title: AI Models Start Building Whole 3D Worlds
dek: Over two months, frontier models went from one-off 3D demos to repeatable pipelines that drive Blender, Unity and Unreal, generate simulations in the browser, and explain machines on demand.
summary: In early September, builders found that GPT-6 Astra could write interactive 3D websites, model objects in Blender through an MCP server, and turn listing photos into 3D houses and videos. The results were striking but mostly one-shot demos, and some builders noted wrong details and the need for explicit design rules to get clean output.

In late September, Opus 5.5 set off a wave of long-running builds in three.js: an ocean simulation that cost $1,874.40 in tokens, an 8-hour cartoon for $173.23, a playable shooter prototype on 15% of a $20 weekly quota, and films written entirely in code. Builders began sharing their prompts, performance passes and open-source libraries, and world models such as Odyssey-3 pointed toward simulation for robots and vehicles.

By October the work turned into tooling. Agent skills like Anatomy turn a one-line machine description into an interactive, rotatable model. MCP connections let Claude Code drive Blender, Unity and Unreal, and a veteran game developer built a headless Blender pipeline that exports rigged assets with collision geometry. Builders also pointed the same methods at factory layouts, warehouse management and floor-plan walkthroughs, while an open-weight DeepSeek model was reported to come close to Opus on Blender and three.js work.

acts.heading: GPT-6 Astra shows a model can build 3D on request

paragraphs.text: The period opens with creative AI still centered on image and video tools, such as an upscaler workflow running in ComfyUI. OpenAI released ChatGPT Images 2.5 on Sep 8 with faster generation, better fidelity and consistent details across multiple edits.

In the first week of September, builders used GPT-6 Astra to produce 3D work directly. One user generated a 3D website that pulls apart a Tesla Model X into 334 modeled pieces. Another had the model download Blender, set up a Blender MCP server and model a photorealistic bat, and it kept iterating until the user ran out of tokens. A third prompted Astra to animate a carton dieline folding into a box inside Blender.

Astra also turned inputs into physical and spatial outputs. One tool turns an image or short idea into a buildable LEGO set using official parts that can be ordered online. Another demo modeled a house in 3D from Zillow listing photos and made a promo video in one shot; the author said some details were still wrong and followed up with an ordinary, unstaged house.

Video and interface work moved too. One builder says Astra plus the Higgsfield MCP generated and edited an 11-minute video in one chat while keeping his face and voice, and another claims Astra with fal's H3 Max makes launch videos in about 5 minutes. Fable 5.1 built an interactive read-aloud children's book with layered 3D illustrations, and GPT 6 Pro built a spreadsheet app with a formula engine and a WebGPU renderer.

Builders learned that quality depended on guardrails. Clean UI came from turning design principles into explicit constraints such as an 8px base grid and iterating component by component. Browser-based design tools also appeared: Pascal Editor, an open-source 3D building editor on React Three Fiber and WebGPU, and a 'Figma for hardware' that treats knobs as configurable hardware components.

acts.heading: World models and multi-tool pipelines appear

paragraphs.text: Odyssey unveiled Odyssey-3, which it calls a foundation world model that can control robots and humanoids, drive cars on Indian roads, pilot drones and play games like GTA. A relaying post notes Odyssey raised $310M three months earlier. Days later, a builder gave Jev an unreleased self-driving world model plus a local segmentation model; it drove, but erratically.

Builders started chaining several models into one scene. A Japanese shrine garden used DeepSeek 4.1 Flash to write prompts, Krea for images, Trellis 2 to convert them to 3D, YuE2 for music and three.js to render. A moonlit swamp with water reflections came from Astra Ultra Code, and a published agent skill for hand-drawn canvas animation produced an example in 16 minutes.

Devin entered the picture when a user had it drive Blender to make a Silicon Valley-style intro video for Dubai. Local, account-free tools also drew attention, such as Photon Studio as a free photo editor that keeps files off the cloud.

acts.heading: Opus 5.5 makes long, costed 3D builds routine

paragraphs.text: Dan Greenheck showed a three.js ocean simulation that cost $1,874.40 in Opus 5.5 tokens, with birds diving and cloth and lights swaying, then shared his full prompt sequence. He also posted a closing prompt that tells the model to optimize GPU and CPU performance with under 1% visual loss until five iterations in a row show negligible gains.

Cost and time became part of each post. A 90s-style cartoon animation in three.js took 7h 58m and $173.23 at max effort. A detailed 3D world came from one prompt in under 8 hours, and a three.js scene with music and generated assets took 40 minutes. One builder says Opus 5.5 built a playable Far Cry 3-style prototype on a $20 plan using about 15% of the weekly quota, then polished it with 21% more; the quoted post claims Opus beat Astra on a 3D benchmark at the same tier.

Some builds were made entirely in code with no assets. Opus 5.5 produced a 5-minute Napoleon battle film, writing the engine, soldiers, score and voice, with terrain from satellite data. IRIS is a 4:52 film generated live by code in one 845 KB HTML file. One user made 20 code-drawn animation styles in two days, and Claude laid a Roman mosaic of 7,446 tiles in browser code with no image model. Meng To steered Opus by asking it to score every part of a code-sculpted ship.

Games and agents multiplied. A No Man's Sky-style game with over 80 planets was built from one prompt on TesanaAI, a Godot prototype from Astra was moved to Unreal, and Opus orchestrated Blender, image generation and three.js into one browser scene. A fishing game in week 9 had Opus handling code and placing ElevenLabs sound effects, with separate sessions per system coordinated by a manager session. A Claude agent with the Runway MCP produced a documentary video on its own.

Supporting libraries and cheaper models followed. Greenheck released Three.js Particle Fluids, an open-source WebGPU library for fluids, cloth, rigid and soft bodies and gases. UniMate offered open-source text-to-animation across different skeletons, and image-to-3dlab's Pixel Match kept text and logos legible on generated models. Matthew Berman claims Sonnet 5.5 is close to Opus 5.5 at 50% lower cost, and showed a 3D ocean simulator with it.

Other builders reused existing code. Opus 5.5 got a repo link for Isaac Mason's new math engine plus one screenshot and built a machine learning visualization in 30 minutes, which Poimandres reshared. Water scenes became a trend, with one built over a few nights with Claude and three.js. Ryan Sael stressed his viral clips are interactive real-time scenes, and a web toy let a stickman destroy any website.

acts.heading: Demos become skills, MCP pipelines and industrial use cases

paragraphs.text: Builders began pointing these methods at operations. Dilum Sanjaya built a warehouse management interface styled like a strategy game with Opus 5.5. Nils Edison rendered a factory floor with machines and worker routines and asked for real factory layouts to simulate. An open-source New York City build offered UE5, Blender and three.js renderers for games, visualization, simulation or reinforcement learning.

The Anatomy skill for Claude turns a one-line machine description into an interactive isometric wireframe you can rotate and inspect, with moving parts and WebGL effects for fire and water. Its repo was published, and users tested it on mechanical switches, a rocket and an espresso machine; one noted the on-screen numbers come from the moving parts. ISO-GLOW, another Claude skill, added three.js scenes and can clean and restyle a user's own .glb model.

Agents moved into professional tools. Guides showed Opus 5.5 working inside the live Unreal Editor and Claude Code connected to Unity and Blender through MCP, with a large spec written first. mixie3D gives agents direct Blender control instead of simulated UI clicks, and one run built a rigged Pegasus. A game developer with 13 years of experience reportedly used Claude Code to build a pipeline where Python drives headless Blender and exports .glb files with rigs, animations and collision geometry.

New 3D formats and generators arrived. Scenario launched an Opus 5.5 based 3D model with clean topology and editable separate parts. An open-source repo reportedly turns one photo into an explorable world with physics meshes, a Gaussian splat and audio in about five minutes. Keenan Crane showed a dragon defined by 27KB of LLM-written GLSL as an implicit surface, and another builder argued implicits may become agents' universal format for 3D modeling and simulation. Enclose.dev added open-source CAD iteration with per-chat version control.

Animation and creative harnesses kept growing. Tripo AI applies plain-English motion descriptions to a 3D model in seconds, and ManimGX launched as an open-source animation engine for agents claiming 90x the speed of ManimCE. A gallery collected 226 Opus 5.5 motion graphics with their prompts, and Voyager launched as an open harness for creative work across Opus, Astra and DeepSeek. Game developers also traded locomotion tips on constraining pelvis and foot direction.

Games and interfaces stretched what runs in a browser. A Japanese boating game with naval combat ran fully in the browser, a Minecraft and Pokemon mashup was reportedly made in one shot with Fable 5.5, a fan built a modern Pokemon gym battle, and a multiplayer Minecraft-style game ran inside an X embed. Rive City showed a full 3D city built in Rive, and Agently pitched screens generated on demand and discarded after use.

Performance and local tools rounded out the stage. Theo relayed an Anthropic post describing how it used Claude to make claude.ai 3x faster in two weeks, with prompts and methods. A webcam-driven site combining Gaussian splatting, MediaPipe and three.js raised the question of how to prove camera data stays local. ImageFlow.dev shipped free in-browser relighting, VoiceStudio offered local voice cloning and dubbing, and design references such as the Michelangelus typeface and the Logo Modernism book circulated.

acts.heading: Pipelines harden and open models close the gap

paragraphs.text: Workflows became repeatable recipes with one job per tool. One guide generates every 3D model with Tripo Smart Mesh P2, then uses Blender, Opus 5.5 and Unity 6 to assemble and code a fishing game. Scenario open-sourced a Blender plugin bundling a '3D team' that Claude Code can control through MCP. Gemini Argon drove Blender MCP in an autonomous loop from a single image to a finished Gothic scene.

Asset quality and supply improved. Pixel Match kept source detail through retopology to about 5k polygons, Summer Engine shipped models that hold up at close zoom, and color-coding each leg fixed a common error in video-to-3D animal animation. Poly Haven's free API gives Claude more than 2,300 models, materials and lighting setups with commercial use allowed.

Applied and large-scale builds followed. Opus 5.5 turned a floor plan into a walkable three.js house, a service the poster says home builders pay $5K to $10K per plan for. Kong Royale, a 50-player battle royale, was built over 3 weeks with chat messages prompting 20 agents overnight. Kaigen3D, a new engine, drew a positive first review, and NPCTalk made GTA V characters answer in cloned voices in under a second.

Audio and design inputs opened up. Fish Audio released Drama 3, an open-weight TTS model with per-word tone control. Designers shared Scrolltide, with 600+ prompts and source code for 3D and scroll-driven sites, plus galleries for navbars, footers and calls to action, as a way to steer models away from generic pages. The period closes with a user reporting that DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 is the first open-weight model that feels close to Opus at Blender and three.js.

A Claude skill called Anatomy turns a one-line description into a rotatable model with moving parts, and people have used it on rockets and espresso machines. customer_angles.for: Platform and tooling leads with existing Blender, Unity or Unreal investments

A veteran game developer used Claude Code to build a pipeline that drives Blender headless and exports assets with rigs and collision geometry, and Devin has been used to drive Blender too. That is a software engineering task, which is where Devin fits.
